existing_checks.scope: PR #4100: compact-switch formalization proposed as future validation.
existing_checks.remaining: Audit the statement and assumptions before a formal proof campaign.

actual_scope: Classify the six-factor paid words equal to the rank-two braid endpoint w=3214 (alphabet D_r(N), r in {s,t,u}, N rank-one), the first open question of PR6642: an all-field sufficiency proof for 16 explicit families and an exhaustive census over F2 and F3 showing these families are every shortest word.
scope_change_reason: The catalogue card asks for one caller-bound formal interface lemma. This package answers the braid-endpoint shortest-word question left open by PR6642 (unpaidmoon), which itself changed scope from the same card. It does not discharge a selected-assumption interface or a Lean binding.
bottleneck_link: Side result for optimal formal words at one braid endpoint. No supplier is priced and the selected conditional value 781451/250000000 is unchanged.
stop_rule: Stop at the family list, its all-field sufficiency certificate and the finite-field completeness census. Do not attempt the all-field completeness proof or a caller invoice in this package.
evidence: verify.py reduces each of the 16 symbolic families to [w] using only the complement/line identity and conjugation, both field-independent; then, over each requested prime field, it enumerates every six-factor word equal to [w] by tight-peel depth-first search with an operator-level final test, and over F2 and F3 also by an unpruned meet-in-the-middle join, and checks that both equal the union of the families, of size 4n^3+12n^2 with n=p(p+1). PROOF.md gives the written argument.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: Are the 16 families every six-factor word for [3214] over every field, including infinite fields and F4?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The census proves completeness only over the fields it enumerates; an all-field classification would make the count 4n^3+12n^2 a theorem for every finite field.
open_questions.first_step: Extend the PR6642 peel table one level: classify tight third peels after each second-peel branch, using the same pair-support method, and show the remainder is forced into a family.
open_questions.blocked_by: After a free second peel the remainder involves two unrelated splittings; the third-peel table has not been derived symbolically.

open_questions.question: Do other rank-two endpoints of length three, such as 1432 or the longest element of S3 on other adjacent pairs, have the same family structure, and what is the general count for a reduced word set of size k?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It would show whether shortest paid words are always generated by complement pairs, line-diagonal blocks and conjugation.
open_questions.first_step: Run the same census with the target permutation changed, over F2 and F3.
open_questions.blocked_by: None for the finite census; the verifier is target-specific only in the constant W.

open_questions.question: What is the complete physical cost of one realization from the two-splitting families (for example s(P) t(X) s(X) t(X') s(X') t(P'))?
open_questions.why_it_matters: These words use only two projector splittings, which may be cheaper to deliver than three.
open_questions.first_step: Fix one caller and its basis-delivery tariff, then compare a two-splitting and a three-splitting family.
open_questions.blocked_by: No tape, precision, stock, compiler or caller tariff is supplied here.
